evidence_grade: B: official City of Monticello pages confirm Scannell's concept-stage proposal, 2025 and 2026 comprehensive-plan actions, no annexation petition, no environmental-review trigger yet, and no formal land-use development application as of the 2026-08-11 refresh; 150 MW is supported only by tracker/local reporting and an official 2025 concept-workshop discussion, not by an approved utility service or interconnection record.
status_as_of_cutoff: Concept-stage / pre-application. The City of Monticello's Scannell Technology Park page states Scannell Properties LLC proposed a 1.3 million-square-foot technology park/data center development on approximately 106 acres, but that the project is at concept stage only and no formal land-use application for development has been received. On 2026-05-26, City Council reguided the western approximately 68 acres of the site to Estate Residential, Low Density Residential, and Mixed Neighborhood; the eastern approximately 38 acres remains Light Industrial Park. No annexation petition, environmental review, rezoning/DCPUD CUP, preliminary/final plat approval, building permit, construction, inspection, CO, utility interconnection, energization, commissioning, or service record was located.

actions.government_body: Monticello Planning Commission and City Council
actions.result_status: The Planning Commission and City Council held a joint workshop to review Scannell's concept. City materials describe concept review as pre-application feedback, not a formal zoning or land-use application.
actions.access_caveat: Concept review is not project approval, land-use entitlement, permit issuance, or construction evidence.
actions.evidence_note: Official city project page and agenda/minutes pathway.

actions.result_status: The city says Council approved Scannell Properties' amendment to guide approximately 76 acres to Light Industrial Park; the remaining approximately 30 acres were already guided Light Industrial Park.
actions.access_caveat: Comprehensive-plan guidance is not final rezoning, CUP, building approval, or construction evidence.

actions.result_status: The city says Council voted to re-analyze the proposed site's land-use guidance and direct the Planning Commission to hold a public hearing concerning high-amenity areas and residential potential.
actions.access_caveat: Direction to re-analyze guidance is not a final project approval.

actions.result_status: The city says Council approved the Data Center Planned Unit Development (DCPUD) ordinance, adding data-center standards to the zoning code. The ordinance regulates future applications; it does not approve Scannell's site.
actions.access_caveat: Citywide ordinance action is not project-specific rezoning, CUP approval, or permit issuance.

actions.result_status: After continuing and closing the public hearing, the Planning Commission voted to recommend City Council approval of re-guiding the western portion of the site back toward residential/mixed-neighborhood categories.
actions.access_caveat: Planning Commission recommendation is not final project approval.

actions.result_status: Council voted to reguide the western approximately 68 acres of the site to Estate Residential, Low Density Residential, and Mixed Neighborhood. The eastern approximately 38 acres abutting Otter Creek Business Park remains Light Industrial Park.
actions.access_caveat: Comprehensive-plan guidance is not final rezoning, CUP, building approval, or construction evidence.
actions.evidence_note: Official city project page; agenda/minutes linked from page.

actions.result_status: The city project page states no annexation petition has been received, environmental review need is determined after an annexation petition, and no formal land-use applications have been received for Scannell's development.
